title: Alt+Tab window not disappearing on Windows after key remapping with PowerToys on Apple keyboard

status.label: Retest the remapped Alt+Tab window switcher on current stable
status.detail: On PowerToys 0.82.1, swapping Win and left Alt reportedly leaves the task switcher visible after the remapped Alt+Tab keys are released; another key dismisses it.

judgment.rationale: The report gives detailed steps on PowerToys 0.82.1: swap Win and left Alt, invoke the task switcher with the remapped Alt+Tab sequence, release both keys, and observe that the switcher remains visible until another key is pressed. The unremapped keys work normally. Open #37519 and closed #18298 also involve Keyboard Manager interactions with the task switcher, but they describe different arrow-key/shortcut effects and do not establish the same defect. Ask whether this exact release-order symptom persists on v0.102.3001 before selecting a fix path.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.82.1 and swaps Win with Left Alt on an Apple keyboard.
After remapped Alt+Tab is released, the task switcher reportedly stays open until another key is pressed; without remapping, it closes normally.
The issue includes a phone video and a detailed reproduction sequence, but no comments or assignees.

Open #37519 describes task-switcher navigation breaking other remapped shortcuts after arrow keys; closed #18298 describes an Alt+arrow mapping closing the switcher. Neither matches this release-order symptom.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask whether the remapped Alt+Tab overlay still remains open on v0.102.3001 after both keys are released.

fix_assessment.rationale: The detailed reproduction is from PowerToys 0.82.1 and current behavior has not been confirmed; related task-switcher reports describe different mappings and outcomes.

issue_context.summary: Swapping Win and Left Alt reportedly causes the task switcher to remain visible after remapped Alt+Tab is released, until another key is pressed.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.82.1 and swaps Win with Left Alt on an Apple keyboard.
The reporter says the remapped Alt+Tab switcher remains visible after releasing both keys and closes only after another key is pressed.
The same switcher closes normally when the keys are not remapped.
There are no comments or assignees; the issue includes a phone video.
inferences: The behavior may relate to modifier release ordering during remapping, but the report does not establish the event path or whether the issue persists in current releases.
issue_context.analysis: Preserve the exact swap and release sequence. The related Alt+Tab reports are not duplicates because they involve different mappings and opposite window-switcher outcomes; a current retest is the next discriminating evidence.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue body, reproduction sequence, labels, and attached video reference.
Compared open #37519 and closed #18298; both concern task-switcher interactions but describe different inputs and outcomes.

information_gaps.information: Whether the task switcher still remains open after releasing remapped Alt+Tab on v0.102.3001 with Win/Left Alt swapped
information_gaps.why_needed: The report is from 0.82.1; a current reproduction is needed to determine whether a remapped modifier-release defect remains.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On v0.102.3001, repeat the documented Win/Left Alt swap and Alt+Tab sequence, then report whether the task switcher closes immediately after both keys are released without an extra keypress.

actions.label: Retest the remapped Alt+Tab window switcher

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed Win/Left Alt swap and Alt+Tab release sequence. Since the report is from PowerToys 0.82.1, could you confirm whether on v0.102.3001 the task switcher still stays open after both remapped keys are released, and whether an extra keypress is still required to dismiss it?
